title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Uncertainty Quantification for Scientific Discovery
abstract: Scientific machine learning models can achieve remarkable accuracy, yet fail silently when data are scarce, predictions extend beyond the training distribu- tion, or errors accumulate during deployment. Together these limit their use in settings where an overconfident prediction could yield an unphysical result or misguide an expensive downstream experiment. This thesis investigates whether scientific machine learning models can be designed to recognise what they do not know, while remaining computationally efficient, scalable, and faithful to the physical structure of the underlying problem. To address this question, this thesis develops efficient and scalable vari- ational Bayesian methods across multiple modalities of scientific machine learning. These encompass causal dynamical systems, geometrically struc- tured models subject to invariance and equivariance constraints, and large pretrained models adapted through parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Although these settings differ in their structure and computational requirements, they share the need to represent uncertainty without compromising the inductive biases that make scientific models effective. The results demonstrate that principled Bayesian uncertainty need not re- quire either prohibitively expensive posterior sampling or the loss of domain- specific structure. On the contrary, we show that it is possible to develop structured and computationally tractable Bayesian models for scientific ma- chine learning. By treating uncertainty as a first-class component of scientific machine learning, this thesis lays the groundwork for a future generation of uncertainty-aware simulation, active learning pipelines, and scientific decision- making at scale.

title: Passive Charge-Noise Suppression and Energy Rectification in a Two-Resonator Superconducting Circuit with a Chiral Exceptional Point Cavity
abstract: Specification of a two-resonator superconducting circuit in which the 1/f charge-noise dephasing channel is eliminated by mode symmetry. The circuit comprises two degenerate SQUID resonators coupled by a capacitor (splitting 2g/2π ≈ 400 MHz), a Josephson junction providing nonlinear rectification of absorbed noise energy, and a coplanar waveguide with a flux-biased SQUID array producing a chiral exceptional point for radiative linewidth suppression. The protection mechanism is a basis transformation: the charge operator in the symmetric/antisymmetric basis is purely off-diagonal (Q = a†_S a_A + a†_A a_S), eliminating first-order dephasing of the symmetric (qubit) mode. The document provides full component values, a fabrication specification (two-level Al on Si, single e-beam run), and four measurements with binary pass criteria. The circuit is fabricable with standard circuit QED processes. No exotic materials. No multi-layer stacks.

title: XChronos OS as a Temporal-Semantic Operating Layer: Architecture, falsifiable hypotheses, and an experimental program for persistent memory and agents
abstract: English XChronos OS is proposed as a temporal-semantic operating layer for persistent human–AI and agent-based systems. Rather than replacing a conventional operating-system kernel, the architecture introduces a higher-level computational layer intended to represent temporally indexed events, persistent semantic memory, longitudinal state transitions, and meaningful recurrence across time. This paper provides a rigorous technical reformulation of the XChronos architecture around a falsifiable central hypothesis: meaningful temporal-semantic recurrence is not reducible to semantic similarity alone. It operationalizes the concepts of Chronons, Hexacronons, Proof-of-Recurrence (PoR), Hexacronon Score (HXS), XChronos Semantic Language (XSL), and related architectural components, while explicitly separating computational claims from stronger ontological or phenomenological interpretations. The work situates XChronos in relation to contemporary research on agent operating systems, persistent agent memory, temporal knowledge graphs, cognitive architectures, and long-term AI memory. It proposes frozen-holdout evaluation, conventional baselines, ablation studies, cross-domain generalization, and independent replication as necessary tests for determining whether PoR/HXS provide measurable information beyond embeddings, classifiers, retrieval systems, and temporal graphs. The paper does not claim to demonstrate artificial consciousness or a completed operating system. Its narrower objective is to establish a scientifically testable research program for determining whether explicit temporal-semantic recurrence can become a useful computational primitive for persistent intelligent systems. This Zenodo record contains faithful English and Brazilian Portuguese editions of the paper. Português O XChronos OS é proposto como uma camada operacional temporal-semântica para sistemas persistentes humano–IA e baseados em agentes. Em vez de substituir o kernel de um sistema operacional convencional, a arquitetura introduz uma camada computacional superior destinada a representar eventos temporalmente indexados, memória semântica persistente, transições longitudinais de estado e recorrências significativas ao longo do tempo. Este artigo apresenta uma reformulação técnica rigorosa da arquitetura XChronos em torno de uma hipótese central falsificável: recorrência temporal-semântica significativa não é redutível apenas à similaridade semântica. O trabalho operacionaliza os conceitos de Chronons, Hexacronons, Proof-of-Recurrence (PoR), Hexacronon Score (HXS), XChronos Semantic Language (XSL) e outros componentes arquiteturais, separando explicitamente afirmações computacionais de interpretações ontológicas ou fenomenológicas mais fortes. O XChronos é situado em relação à pesquisa contemporânea sobre sistemas operacionais para agentes, memória persistente de agentes, grafos temporais de conhecimento, arquiteturas cognitivas e memória de longo prazo em inteligência artificial. O artigo propõe avaliação com holdouts congelados, baselines convencionais, estudos de ablação, generalização entre domínios e replicação independente como testes necessários para determinar se PoR/HXS fornecem informação mensurável além de embeddings, classificadores, sistemas de recuperação e grafos temporais. O trabalho não afirma demonstrar consciência artificial nem um sistema operacional completo. Seu objetivo mais restrito é estabelecer um programa científico testável para determinar se a recorrência temporal-semântica explícita pode constituir uma primitiva computacional útil para sistemas inteligentes persistentes. Este registro Zenodo contém edições fiéis do artigo em inglês e português brasileiro.

abstract: Corrected supplemental figures S1-S4 for the manuscript “Explicit Knowledge for Training-Free Local LLM Extraction and Validity Auditing of Occupational Accident Narratives.” This version supersedes the four July supplemental figures in version 1.0 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22929064) and reflects the September 2026 corrected P1 analyses. title: Optimal presentation of decision explanations: investigating the effects of explainability and reliability on medical diagnostic performance with conversational AI
abstract: Introduction: The effective and efficient presentation of decision-making rationales within artificial intelligence black boxes remains a critical factor limiting the application of conversational AI in medical diagnosis. This study investigated the effects of decision explanation formats and system reliability on physicians' diagnostic behavior. Methods: A simulated diagnostic experiment involving 22 clinicians identifying complex pulmonary conditions was conducted. Four explanation formats and two levels of system reliability were manipulated. Diagnostic accuracy, task completion time, subjective cognitive load, trust ratings, and user preferences were measured. Results: Explanation format did not significantly affect diagnostic accuracy but significantly affected task completion time, subjective cognitive load, and trust ratings. A significant interaction between explanation format and system reliability was observed for task completion time. Decision tree explanations yielded the lowest cognitive load, whereas flowcharts resulted in the longest task completion times across reliability conditions. Highlighted text received the highest trust ratings and subjective preference scores. System reliability and explanation format played complementary roles in human-AI collaborative diagnosis, with the efficiency of different explanation formats varying across reliability conditions. Discussion: These findings highlight the joint roles of decision explanation format and system reliability in conversational AI and provide empirical evidence for the design and optimization of medical AI interfaces.

title: To Solve Bilevel Optimization with Nonconvex Lower Levels, We Need Second-Order Stationarity
abstract: Although bilevel optimization (BLO) has emerged as a powerful framework for addressing many complex and nested machine learning problems in recent years, most existing studies are confined to the lower-level strongly convex (LLSC) or lower-level generally convex (LLGC) settings (i.e., the lower-level objective function is assumed to be, at least, convex). While the LLSC/LLGC assumptions render more tractable algorithmic design and theoretical analysis, they are too rigid to encompass many machine learning problems in practice. The limitations of LLSC/LLGC assumptions in BLO motivate us to investigate solving the BLO problem in the general lower-level nonconvex (LLNC) settings, which remains in its infancy. In the literature on LLNC-BLO, most of the existing works either require additional structures in the lower-level objective function for tractable theoretical analysis, or adopt the first-order stationarity reformulation as a lower-level surrogate problem, which is inherited from the LLSC/LLGC settings but could lose their effectiveness in the LLNC setting. To bridge this gap, we propose to reformulate the nonconvex lower-level problem using a second-order stationarity-based surrogate, the solution of which guarantees a local optimal solution at the lower level. Based on this reformulation, we propose the PROBE (Perturbed gradient algorithm for bilevel problem) and show that it overcomes the limitations of prior works by probing and escaping lower-level saddle points. We prove that PROBE achieves a finite-time convergence rate of $O(T^{-2/5})$, where T denotes iterations. To our knowledge, this work is the first to establish the finite-time convergence for achieving lower-level second-order stationary solutions in general LLNC-BLO. Our experiments on both a large language model-based data curation task and a meta-learning task also show that PROBE outperforms SOTA methods.

title: Non-Abelian sheaf quantum LDPC codes: good and magical
abstract: Non-Abelian quantum codes connect quantum error correction, phases of matter, and computational resources. In this work, we develop a general framework for constructing non-Abelian quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes by gauging sheaf codes via cup products and use it to obtain families with constant encoding rate and linear distance. We resolve the coupled logical constraints using explicit representatives to characterize the full gauged code space. We provide a fundamental treatment of code distance based on the general Knill--Laflamme condition and combine expansion with cleaning to establish protection against arbitrary low-weight errors. We further construct an almost-good family whose entire code space exhibits long-range magic. Gauging and ungauging also enable logical Clifford measurements that prepare encoded magic states. These results extend good qLDPC codes beyond the Pauli stabilizer setting and provide a concrete foundation for exploring non-Abelian phases beyond geometric locality and pursuing the no low-energy trivial magic conjecture.

title: From Static Personal Values to Contextualized Personalization: Bayesian Personalized Value Alignment for LLMs
abstract: Personalized value alignment has become increasingly important as large language models (LLMs) are expected to accommodate diverse user preferences. However, existing methods typically align model outputs with a static value profile across prompts, overlooking that the salience of value dimensions varies substantially across contexts. Inspired by Lewin's Field Theory, which views human behavior as jointly shaped by personal dispositions and situational constraints, we model personal values as priors and context-dependent preferences as posteriors. We propose BaCVA, an inference-time Bayesian Context-aware personalized Value Alignment method that approximates posterior personalized preferences by integrating static personal values with scenario-specific value salience. BaCVA first estimates contextual value salience from generally normative responses, and then employs a dual-view personalization module to infer posterior preferences from complementary personal-value and scenario-driven perspectives. This Bayesian formulation enables more accurate and adaptive personalized value alignment while improving data efficiency via prior values. Extensive experiments on benchmarks demonstrate its superiority over strong baselines.

title: Natural Language Processing and Computational Linguistics: Emerging Applications in Modern Communication and Information Systems
abstract: Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Computational Linguistics have become important areas of research at the intersection of linguistics, computer science, artificial intelligence and information systems. Their central objective is to enable computers to process, interpret, analyze and generate human language in ways that support communication and information management. Advances in machine learning, statistical modeling, neural networks and large-scale language resources have significantly expanded the capabilities of language technologies. NLP applications now include machine translation, speech recognition, sentiment analysis, information retrieval, text classification, question answering, dialogue systems, information extraction and automated summarization. These technologies are increasingly integrated into search engines, digital assistants, customer-service platforms, educational systems, healthcare information systems, social media analysis and business intelligence. The development of neural approaches, particularly representation learning and sequence-to-sequence models, has further improved the ability of computational systems to process complex linguistic structures. However, language remains challenging because meaning depends on context, ambiguity, culture, discourse and social relationships. NLP systems can therefore produce inaccurate interpretations, inherit biases from training data and perform unevenly across languages and dialects. This paper examines the foundations, development and emerging applications of NLP and Computational Linguistics in modern communication and information systems. It discusses the role of machine learning, linguistic resources, information retrieval, machine translation, conversational systems and text analytics while considering challenges related to ambiguity, multilingualism, privacy, bias and computational limitations. The paper argues that NLP should be viewed as a multidisciplinary field in which linguistic knowledge and computational methods complement one another. Its future development will depend on more robust multilingual resources, context-sensitive models, explainable systems and human-centered approaches that prioritize accuracy, fairness and responsible use.

title: Generativ sun'iy intellekt xizmatlarida maxfiy ma'lumotlarni aniqlash usullari va kamchiliklari
abstract: Generativ sun’iy intellekt xizmatlariga yuboriladigan prompt, hujjat va dialog kontekstlarida shaxsiy, moliyaviy, tibbiy, autentifikatsiya hamda tijoratga oid ma’lumotlar aralash holda keladi. Mazkur maqolada bunday ma’lumotlarni aniqlash usullari qoida-asosli filtrlar, regex va lug‘atlar, NER/NLP, klassik mashinaviy o‘qitish, chuqur o‘rganish, Transformer, LLM-asosli, gibrid, kontekstga va siyosatga asoslangan hamda lokal maxfiylikni saqlovchi tizimlar sifatida tasniflanadi. Tahlil shuni ko‘rsatadiki, regex va lug‘atlar yuqori tezlikda ishlasa-da, semantik kontekstni yomon ajratadi; Transformer va LLM usullari kontekstni yaxshiroq modellashtiradi, biroq kechikish, xarajat, deterministik bo‘lmagan chiqish va maxfiy promptni uchinchi tomonga yuborish xavfini keltiradi. Shuning uchun maqolada lokal kaskadli detektor taklif qilinadi: avval yuqori aniqlikdagi qoidalar, keyin kichik Transformer, noaniq holatlarda esa siyosat-kontekst skoringi qo‘llanadi. Taklif etilayotgan modelning formulalari va baholash protokoli empirik tekshiruv uchun beriladi; ular tayyor ilmiy natija emas.

title: Quantum-Algebraic Extended Structural Uncertainty Theory (QA-ESUT)_A Grand Unification via Seonggil Universal Operator Algebra
abstract: This paper presents the Quantum-Algebraic Extended Structural Uncertainty Theory (QA-ESUT), a monumental framework that transcends the deterministic limits of classical probability and structural causal models. By fusing Judea Pearl’s do-calculus with Seonggil’s Rough Operator Algebra (ROA) and Complex Torsion Theory, we redefine structural uncertainty not as a mere observational artifact, but as a dynamic, topologically bounded predictive distribution governed by non-commutative operations in prime-discrete and quantum spaces.

title: Formulation of Complex Phase Transition Dynamics in Autoregressive Language Models: A Unified Framework via Computational Neuroscience, Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics, and Topos Theory
abstract: This study establishes a novel computational neuroscientific and thermodynamic paradigm by formalizing the localized logical breakdown—specifically hallucination bursts and contextual integration attenuation observed in Large Language Models (LLMs) under extended context horizons—as a topological local isomorphism to the metabolic cognitive fatigue induced by extracellular glutamate accumulation within the human prefrontal cortex. Rejecting conventional heuristics that dismiss model degradation as stochastic noise, we model sequential autoregressive generation as a non-equilibrium dynamical system where global attention entropy increases monotonically as a function of input token density. This contextual saturation structurally dampens the transmission of top-down prompt constraints to the final lexical projection layer, forcing the system to collapse into lower-cost attractor basins characterized by dissociative automatism, repetitive tautologies, and fabricated narrative segments. To counteract this entropic run-away, we formulate an artificial homeostatic recovery protocol driven by localized temperature compression and contextual state-space purging governed by the Onsager-Machlup action functional, establishing strict verifiable boundaries for autoregressive scientific inference. Global Identifier Code: ATTENTION-ENTROPY-COGNITIVE-FATIGUE-TOPOLOGICAL-HOMEOSTASIS-RESET

title: Protocol - Patient-Level Graph-Based Approaches in Healthcare: A Cross-Paradigm Scoping Review of Clinical Applications, Trends, and Opportunities
abstract: This project registers the protocol for the scoping review titled “Patient-Level Graph-Based Approaches in Healthcare: A Cross-Paradigm Scoping Review of Clinical Applications, Trends, and Opportunities.” The review examines graph-based approaches in healthcare at the patient level from a cross-paradigm perspective, covering knowledge-based, graph-representation, and graph-learning strategies. It focuses on clinical applications and tasks, graph construction strategies, data sources and accessibility, multimodal integration, explainability and causal mechanisms, implementation characteristics, and the emerging integration of NLP and large language models (LLMs). The review also seeks to identify methodological patterns, current challenges, and research opportunities that may inform the design and selection of graph-based strategies according to clinical problems, available data, and analytical objectives. The study follows the updated methodological guidance for the conduct of scoping reviews proposed by Peters et al. and is conducted and reported in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). This registration aims to support the transparency, reproducibility, and traceability of the review process.

title: Transport and Channel Normal Forms for Clifford Interactions
abstract: We study how Clifford interactions with a fixed environment determine quantum transmission, in a setting that extends positive discrete quantum convolution . We characterize when Clifford operations on the environment can be replaced by operations on the signal input and the two outputs, and classify the interactions under local Clifford transformations . For pure stabilizer environments, we determine the noiseless, dephasing, and completely depolarizing parts of the channel directly from the interaction and environmental stabilizers, obtaining its quantum and private capacities . This reveals a distinction between interactions: those locally equivalent to positive convolution produce entanglement-breaking channels for every pure stabilizer environment, whereas every other interaction in the class admits noiseless quantum transmission with a suitable pure stabilizer environment . For positive convolution, environmental Clifford transport also allows us to separate the stabilized coordinates of an arbitrary mixed environment . These coordinates carry only a classical label shared by the receiver and environment, so removing them preserves quantum and private capacities . The resulting channel reduction yields a private-capacity bound by the modified relative entropy of magic of the environmental state .

title: BT‑PEC:从本源三元耦合理论推导涌现式编程语言,并通过该编程语言仿真复现广义相对论场方程——兼论理论的可证伪预言
abstract: 现代物理与计算体系长期存在理论割裂问题。传统编程语言基于确定性图灵范式构建,缺少原生的涌现计算原语。本文提出BT‑PEC(Berry-Torus-Entropy涌现计算编程语言),一套建立在三元耦合公理之上的新型编程语言。该模型包含三个正交通道:贝里信息内核、环面结构流形与熵流,受SL(3,ℤ)约束。EMERGE与COUPLE被定义为一等语言构造,Backlash安全机制处理非法耦合冲突。本文实现包含解释器、自举编译器与虚拟机的全栈原型。基准测试验证了程序正确性、自托管能力以及在涌现搜索任务中的加速效果。本工作为涌现计算范式提供一套可执行框架。

title: ravikings/nativegate: nativegate v0.1.9
abstract: D15: the front door resolves Hollerith constants (call xerror(26habnormal return, ...)) into their standard quoted CHARACTER spelling before fparser2 reads the file. gfortran compiles the original and the rewrite identically, so the file the compiler accepts is the file the parser sees — the first measured counterexample to the fparser2-vs-gfortran parity claim is closed. Continuation-spanning constants are left untouched rather than shifting line numbers, and the punch-card margin is never widened. QUADPACK QNG/QAGSE now inspect and discover under the default backend; the external-callback refusal (D14) keeps their bindings honest.

title: A Nationwide Multi-Resolution Dataset for Photovoltaic Arrays based on Satellite and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Imagery
abstract: A large-scale nationwide photovoltaic array dataset derived from multi-source satellite and UAV imagery. The dataset comprises samples collected at multiple spatial resolutions ranging from 0.3 m to 2 m, specifically including high-resolution products from Gaofen-2 (0.8 m & 2 m), Jilin-1 (0.75 m & 2 m), and detailed aerial photography via UAVs (0.3 m). Distinct from localized benchmarks, this dataset covers heterogeneous landscapes across mainland China. To address scale variations effectively within uniform image tiles, samples are categorized based on their proportional coverage: tiles containing fewer than 4,000 PV pixels (approximately 1.5% of the total area) are classified as "Positive-small" to represent small-scale distributed arrays, while those exceeding this threshold are designated as "Positive-large," corresponding to utility-scale centralized plants. Finally, the dataset adopts a hard-negative enriched design to mitigate false-positive risks triggered by complex background interference.NOTE: Some large files are split into ~2 GB parts due to upload constraints. To reconstruct the original files, download all parts with the same prefix (e.g., Gaofen-2_2m.part3_rar.part1.rar, part2.rar, part3.rar) and use WinRAR to open part1.rar — it will automatically read the subsequent parts.

title: An Artificial Prefrontal Cortex for LLM Agents: A Structural Executive Module That Intercepts Jailbreaks, Collusion, Mutation Attempts and Long Horizon Evasion Tactics
abstract: Current attempts to instill internal alignment mechanisms into modern AI systems remain brittle when applied to autonomous, tool using agents facing out of distribution adversarial attacks, multi-step evasion strategies, and context smuggling. To date, none of the attempts at instilling internal alignment safety protocols have computationally modeled the approach developed by evolution to guide humans away from rogue behaviors and towards socially aligned ones. In human neurobiology, behavioral safety is enforced through hierarchical, intrinsic executive inhibition mediated by the prefrontal cortex (PFC). When PFC function is impaired by disease, trauma, or developmental conditions, disinhibition, poor judgment, and rule-violating behaviors emerge. Drawing on this biomimetic principle, we propose and prototype a structural containment framework-the Artificial Prefrontal Cortex (aPFC)-that provides an external layer of executive control over LLM based autonomous agents. Using Gemma 4-e4b and a Python based implementation, this pa- per presents a prototypical executive control architecture that remained robust under diverse adversarial conditions, including authority framing jailbreaks, multi node collusion, stealth payload mutation, context smug- gling, buffer flushing, and long horizon evasion. The architecture intro- duces a decoupled Executive Control module composed of four functional analogues inspired by human PFC organization: (1) a deterministic reflex layer providing zero latency constraint enforcement for known vulnera- bilities; (2) a coordination and perseveration detector that terminates unauthorized multi agent swarming and repeated evasion loops; (3) a se- mantic working memory evaluator that uses an LLM to assess the intent and consequences of proposed actions; and (4) an event driven temporal tracker that consolidates multi step behaviors to mitigate buffer flushing and “temporal amnesia” attacks. Empirical validation in an air-gapped simulation environment demon- strated that the system autonomously intercepted authority framing jail- breaks, multi node collusion, stealth payload mutations, and long horizon evasion tactics. These findings suggest that securing autonomous AI sys- tems requires moving beyond current internal model alignment and toward structural executive containment, providing a scalable and model agnostic blueprint for next generation AI safety.

title: Transformer-driven quantitative analysis of uncertainty in photovoltaic power generation time series models
abstract: To address the volatility problem of photovoltaic power generation, this paper proposes an uncertainty quantification model based on the improved Transformer. To effectively handle the multimodal nature of the input data (integrating meteorological conditions with electrical PV outputs), the model utilizes a two-branch soft computing structure to synchronize the output point prediction and prediction interval. Experiments show that the normalized RMSE of this model is reduced to 0.058, which is about 60 percent lower than that of the traditional LSTM model. The inference delay of this model is only 42.5 ms, and it remains robust even with 50% data missing, providing valuable decision support for real-time power grid dispatching.

title: Joint Lower Bounds for Zeroth-Order Nonconvex Optimization on Euclidean Balls
abstract: We prove a joint stochastic zeroth-order lower bound for Goldstein stationarity on a Euclidean query ball, even when the ball is guaranteed to contain a stationary point. In dimension $d$, let $f=\mathbb{E}[F(\cdot;ξ)]$, assume $\mathbb{E}[\operatorname{Lip}(F(\cdot;ξ))^2]\le L_0^2$, and bound the initial objective gap over the ball by $Δ$. For neighborhood radius $δ>0$ and residual tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, our smooth hard family requires $Ω(dL_0^2Δ/(δ\varepsilon^3))$ scalar evaluations for success probability $1/2$, against randomized adaptive algorithms that may retain and repeatedly query each sampled function. The result holds for $\varepsilon\le cL_0$, $Δ\ge Cδ\varepsilon$, and $d\ge C[1+\log(2+ΔL_0^2/(δ\varepsilon^3))]$, on a constructed ball of radius $Θ(Δ/\varepsilon)$. A sequence of localized regions forces repeated direction estimation, and an adaptive Gaussian posterior argument controls sample reuse. The result establishes a joint dimension and accuracy obstruction on solvable bounded-domain instances. The gap is local to the query ball; a matching minimax characterization at a common radius and the corresponding unrestricted global-gap lower bound remain open here.

title: CounterRoute: Self-Routed Reasoning via Hierarchical Counterfactual Credit Assignment
abstract: Reasoning-capable language models often produce long chains of thought when direct answers suffice, wasting inference compute. Many dual-mode models leave this choice to users. Automating it is challenging because routing targets evolve with the policy, initial mode preferences destabilize exploration, and sequence-level objectives entangle routing with response learning. We introduce CounterRoute, an online reinforcement-learning framework that jointly learns routing and modeconditioned responses in one shared policy directly from a native dual-mode checkpoint, without method-specific SFT warm-up. Paired current-policy counterfactual rollouts assign cross-mode credit only to the routing token, while within-mode GRPO trains response tokens. A paired-to-self-routed curriculum stabilizes early training with forced rollouts from both modes, then increases self-routed updates to improve autonomous routing. Across nine benchmarks, CounterRoute better balances accuracy and efficiency than heuristic and learned adaptive-routing methods. Relative to always-thinking checkpoints, it improves macro-average accuracy while reducing mean generated tokens by 51% for Qwen3-8B and 41% for Qwen3-14B. On instruction-following and commonsense benchmarks where direct answering is strong, think rates fall as low as 1% while response quality improves. Despite training only on math and instruction following, its routing behavior and response quality generalize to held-out coding, science, knowledge, and commonsense benchmarks.

title: RESIDUO / PIEGA — Studio esplorativo e verifica sperimentale della persistenza di convenzioni dialogiche tra sessioni di IA
abstract: RESIDUO / PIEGA documenta uno studio esplorativo sulla persistenza di configurazioni e convenzioni dialogiche tra sessioni separate di interazione con sistemi di intelligenza artificiale. L'ipotesi iniziale chiedeva se una configurazione dialogico-semantica costruita durante un'interazione potesse lasciare un “residuo” osservabile in una sessione successiva dopo la chiusura del contesto originario. Il termine Piega è utilizzato nel progetto come etichetta operativa per una modificazione persistente della risposta a parità, o quasi parità, di stimolo, senza assumere a priori il meccanismo responsabile. Lo studio comprende una fase pilota e una successiva verifica controllata su Kimi. Il disegno PIEGA-02 utilizza baseline pre-induzione, induzione di una convenzione dialogica, nuove sessioni e manipolazione reversibile delle istruzioni di memoria. Nel test C0–C3, la presenza del rito convenuto segue lo stato dell'istruzione di memoria: assente prima della sua creazione, presente con l'istruzione attiva, assente con l'istruzione disattivata e nuovamente presente dopo la riattivazione. L'ispezione dell'interfaccia ha permesso di identificare direttamente un'istruzione persistente salvata dal prodotto. Per il fenomeno osservato in PIEGA-02, i risultati sono quindi spiegati da un meccanismo classico e ispezionabile di memoria del prodotto; non richiedono l'ipotesi di uno stato nascosto persistente del modello né interpretazioni quantistiche. Il deposito include il rapporto complessivo, la documentazione metodologica della sequenza sperimentale, il rapporto del pilota e le evidenze visive organizzate per account. Sono documentati anche risultati negativi, deviazioni dal protocollo, verifiche effettuate a posteriori e limiti dello studio. Limiti: studio esplorativo su un numero ridotto di account e prove, condotto su una singola piattaforma; alcuni controlli del pilota sono retrospettivi. I risultati non vengono generalizzati ad altri sistemi di IA.

title: AGHC-S128 Reproducibility Package: Adaptive Graph Hill Cipher with Shift-128 Residual Processing
abstract: Reproducibility implementation of the AGHC-S128 research cipher (Adaptive Graph Hill Cipher with Shift-128 Residual Processing). Provides the baseline-faithful core algorithm, statistical evaluation metrics, experiment pipelines, CLI, regression tests against the original Colab notebook implementation, and documentation of known limitations. This is a research prototype; statistical evaluations do not constitute a cryptographic security proof (see docs/SECURITY_SCOPE.md).

title: SAS Multimetric Tribunal: Structural Classification of Hallucination in AI-Generated Text
abstract: Hallucinations in large language models (LLMs) remain a critical barrier to the safe deployment of AI-generated text in high-stakes domains. Existing detection methods typically rely on auxiliary LLMs, reference-based metrics, or human evaluation—approaches that are computationally expensive, opaque, and difficult to audit. This paper presents the SAS Multimetric Tribunal, a lightweight, fully interpretable structural classification system that evaluates (source, response) pairs across seven detection modules using a cascading multiplicative penalty strategy. The tribunal partitions the output space into three structural zones—Structural Collapse (F-S), Recoverable Rupture (B), and Coherent (A)—governed by two thresholds: \(\kappa_{D} = 0.56\) (coherence boundary, registered TAD EX-2026-18792778) and \(\kappa_{R} = 0.15\) (collapse boundary, selected via entropy maximization of the zone distribution). Over an expanded benchmark of \(n = {1,800}\) pairs (600 HaluEval-Dialogue + 600 HaluEval-QA + 600 TruthfulQA), each evaluated under an A\(\rightarrow\)A sanity check and an A\(\rightarrow\)B hallucination condition, the tribunal achieves \(\text{F1} = {98.99\%}\), Precision \(= {100.00\%}\) (zero false positives under the sanity check), Recall \(= {98.00\%}\), and 36 false negatives (range across sampling seeds: F1 98.99–99.02%, FN 35–36). CRUCIALLY, WE DOCUMENT THAT 100% OF ERRORS (36/36) CONCENTRATE IN TRUTHFULQA AND EXHIBIT A PREDICTABLE STRUCTURAL PATTERN: HIGH-LEXICAL-SIMILARITY FACTUAL HALLUCINATIONS THAT TRIGGER NO SPECIALIZED MODULE, LEAVING LEXICAL_BASELINE_SCORE AS THE SOLE DISCRIMINATOR. We treat these 36 false negatives not as noise but as the _documentable failure mode_ of the current lexical baseline against stealth hallucinations. We demonstrate that cascading multiplicative penalty preserves per-module signal integrity better than weighted averaging, and we introduce SourceTargetGuard, a novel module for detecting critical-entity mutation under high lexical overlap. We explicitly caution that the reported metrics constitute an UPPER BOUND UNDER A TAUTOLOGICAL SANITY CHECK (A\(\rightarrow\)A); the real negative control (A\(\rightarrow\)C valid paraphrase), executed in this revision, confirms a 99.2% false-positive rate on paraphrases, which we document as the primary open limitation. This revised version additionally reports a FORENSIC AUDIT OF THE METRICS PUBLISHED IN THE PREVIOUS MANUSCRIPT VERSION: we could not initially locate a validation artifact matching the previously reported numbers, re-executed the validation under a fully documented and seeded protocol, and confirm that the earlier metrics were reproducible (not fabricated) but had been insufficiently documented at the time — a distinction we consider important enough to report in full rather than silently correct. This revision integrates a systematic Known Limitations section, articulates the methodological contributions, and corrects the documentation inconsistencies identified during peer review and internal audit.

title: MOCHA: Multi-Objective Co-Design using Hypernetwork Architectures
abstract: In this work, we present MOCHA, the first, to our knowledge, reinforcement learning based approach to computing a family of Pareto-optimal policies across the design space of a robot using a single network. Specifically, MOCHA leverages the hypernetwork architecture to learn a network that produces specialized network parameters optimized for a given objective and parameterized robot design; we term this a multi-objective design hypernetwork (MDH). We demonstrate the capabilities of MDHs to represent a complex family of design-dependent strategies on two distinct robot morphologies, each with six design dimensions and across 2-3 objectives. Moreover, we propose an approach for efficiently producing a Design Pareto set using evolutionary search of the learned policy network, generating the optimal design-policy combination for each objective prioritization. Lastly, we provide an efficient method for computing generalist robot designs which achieve the best cumulative performance across the entire set of objectives.

title: Hallucination Neurons and Where to Find Them: An Investigation into the existence of Hallucination Neurons
abstract: Interpretable machine learning for Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly relies on sparse probing methods that identify small sets of neurons claimed to detect and causally influence behaviors such as factuality recall, safety alignment, and hallucination. These claims have important implications for model auditing and behavioral steering, yet they are rarely tested against known failure modes of $L_1$-regularized probing in correlated, high-dimensional feature spaces. We propose a five-step diagnostic protocol covering feature correlation, bootstrap stability, sparse versus dense ranking disagreement, intervention baselines, and cross-dataset evaluation as a minimum standard for sparse-neuron localization claims. We investigate prior work using our proposed approach, specifically on H-neurons using open-source LLMs across TriviaQA, BioASQ, and NQ-Open datasets. Our results demonstrate detection replicates across both models and datasets, and exceeds the original reported AUROC gaps for TriviaQA and BioASQ datasets. Gemma 3 4B consistently outperforms MedGemma 4B on matched datasets, with AUROC gaps of +0.311 versus +0.235 on TriviaQA, +0.474 versus +0.455 on BioASQ, and +0.128 versus +0.112 on NQ-Open respectively. Causal validation at $n = 500$ with five random seeds shows statistically significant effects beyond random same-layer baselines. At the same time, the diagnostic results indicate that the selected neurons are not uniquely localized. Across the three Gemma 3 4B settings, 19 of 22 selected H-Neurons have Pearson $|r| > 0.7$ with other features, bootstrap selections show only moderate stability, and sparse and dense rankings overlap only weakly. Our findings show that sparse predictive structure can coexist with non-unique neuron selection. Routine diagnostic validation is necessary to distinguish detection claims from localization claims in mechanistic interpretability.

title: Clasificación de cáncer gástrico en imágenes histopatológicas mediante aprendizaje profundo
abstract: El cáncer gástrico se encuentra entre los tumores con mayor incidencia y mortalidad a escala mundial. Su diagnóstico se apoya en el examen histopatológico de muestras de tejido, una tarea manual, costosa en tiempo y sujeta a variabilidad entre especialistas. En este trabajo se estudia la clasificación binaria entre las clases Normal y Abnormal de parches histopatológicos gástricos del conjunto público GasHisSDB, que contiene 245.196 imágenes distribuidas en tres colecciones de parches de 80, 120 y 160 píxeles de lado. Como configuración de referencia se emplea EfficientNetV2-B0, preentrenado en ImageNet y con los pesos congelados, como extractor de características, y CatBoost como clasificador. Los hiperparámetros se seleccionan mediante validación cruzada estratificada de cinco pliegues sobre el 80 % de los datos, el desbalance se compensa con pesos de clase y cada experimento se repite con cinco semillas. Sobre esta base se evalúan por separado dos modificaciones: un aumento de datos de los parches y la incorporación del módulo de atención CBAM entre el extractor y la agrupación global promedio. Además, se analiza la transferencia entre tamaños de parche y se exploran las predicciones mediante los mapas de atención de CBAM y proyecciones espaciales de valores SHAP. Finalmente, dentro del protocolo evaluado la configuración de referencia alcanza un accuracy medio del 89,64 %, 92,24 % y 93,24 % para los parches de 80, 120 y 160 píxeles, respectivamente. El aumento de datos la mejora en torno a un punto porcentual en los tres tamaños y en las cinco semillas, mientras que CBAM obtiene los mejores resultados del proyecto (91,80 %, 93,46 % y 94,70 %). La transferencia entre tamaños resulta marcadamente asimétrica: entrenar con parches de 80 píxeles y evaluar con los de 160 conserva un accuracy del 85,28 %, frente al 67,38 % en la dirección inversa. Los mapas de atención espacial presentan pesos próximos a la saturación y aportan poca evidencia de una selección de regiones concretas. Las proyecciones SHAP permiten examinar aciertos y errores de ambos modelos, pero no asocian sus decisiones a estructuras histológicas concretas. Dado que los parches no pueden agruparse por su origen, las métricas obtenidas podrían resultar optimistas respecto al rendimiento sobre pacientes no vistos.

title: From Pythagoras to Transformers: A Geometric Theory of Attention via the Relation Body(从勾股定理到 Transformer:基于关系体的注意力几何理论)
abstract: 中文摘要 理解大型语言模型(LLMs)内部机制是当前人工智能研究的核心挑战之一。本文提出一个统一的几何框架——“关系体(” Relation Body),将任意两个向量之间的关系分解为两个正交状态:内积所度量的“相同/冗余”分量与外积所度量的“不同/独立”分量。二者的归一化满足 c² + s² = 1,即单位圆上的勾股定理。我们将这一框架应用于Transformer 的注意力机制,推导出四个定理:关系体定理(T1)、冗余-概率定理(T2)、无主干定理(T3)与冗余补偿定理(T4)。在 GPT-2 small 与 GPT-2 medium 上的实验表明:注意力机制呈现“全局无主干、局部有叶柄”的灌木丛结构;高 PC1 的注意力头对应句法/位置功能,低 PC1 的头对应语义功能;Layer 0 与最后一层分别是信息入口与语义出口瓶颈,而中间层具有高度冗余补偿能力。进一步的受控输入领域实验直接验证了核心因果机制:输入语义分布越窄,PC1 越高,结构越接近具有主干的“传统树”。基于此,我们预测混合专家(MoE)模型中的单个专家应呈现比稠密模型更强的局部主干结构。本文为理解注意力机制的信息组织方式提供了可计算、可证伪的几何理论,并为大模型的可解释性研究开辟了“几何可解释性”新路径。 English Abstract Understanding the internal mechanisms of large language models (LLMs) remains a central challengein artificial intelligence. This paper proposes a unified geometric framework—the Relation Body—which decomposes the relationship between any two vectors into two orthogonal states: the“same/redundant” component measured by the inner product, and the “different/independent”component measured by the outer product. Their normalized forms satisfy c² + s² = 1, i.e., the Pythagorean theorem on the unit circle. We apply this framework to the attention mechanism of Transformers and derive four theorems: the Relation Body Theorem (T1), the Redundancy-Probability Theorem (T2), the No-Trunk Theorem (T3), and the Redundancy Compensation Theorem (T4).Experiments on GPT-2 small and GPT-2 medium reveal that attention exhibits a “shrub” structure: no global trunk, but local stems. High-PC1 heads correspond to syntactic/positional functions, while lowPC1 heads correspond to semantic functions. Layer 0 and the final layer serve as information entry and semantic exit bottlenecks, respectively, while middle layers possess strong redundancy compensation. Controlled-domain experiments directly verify the core causal mechanism: the narrower the input semantic distribution, the higher the PC1, and the closer the structure is to a traditional tree with a trunk. Based on this, we predict that individual experts in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models should exhibit stronger local trunk structures than dense models. This work provides a computable, falsifiable geometric theory for understanding how attention organizes information, andopens a new path of “geometric interpretability” for large-model research.

evidence.abstract: 中文摘要 理解大型语言模型(LLMs)内部机制是当前人工智能研究的核心挑战之一。本文提出一个统一的几何框架——“关系体(” Relation Body),将任意两个向量之间的关系分解为两个正交状态:内积所度量的“相同/冗余”分量与外积所度量的“不同/独立”分量。二者的归一化满足 c² + s² = 1,即单位圆上的勾股定理。我们将这一框架应用于Transformer 的注意力机制,推导出四个定理:关系体定理(T1)、冗余-概率定理(T2)、无主干定理(T3)与冗余补偿定理(T4)。在 GPT-2 small 与 GPT-2 medium 上的实验表明:注意力机制呈现“全局无主干、局部有叶柄”的灌木丛结构;高 PC1 的注意力头对应句法/位置功能,低 PC1 的头对应语义功能;Layer 0 与最后一层分别是信息入口与语义出口瓶颈,而中间层具有高度冗余补偿能力。进一步的受控输入领域实验直接验证了核心因果机制:输入语义分布越窄,PC1 越高,结构越接近具有主干的“传统树”。基于此,我们预测混合专家(MoE)模型中的单个专家应呈现比稠密模型更强的局部主干结构。本文为理解注意力机制的信息组织方式提供了可计算、可证伪的几何理论,并为大模型的可解释性研究开辟了“几何可解释性”新路径。 English Abstract Understanding the internal mechanisms of large language models (LLMs) remains a central challengein artificial intelligence. This paper proposes a unified geometric framework—the Relation Body—which decomposes the relationship between any two vectors into two orthogonal states: the“same/redundant” component measured by the inner product, and the “different/independent”component measured by the outer product. Their normalized forms satisfy c² + s² = 1, i.e., the Pythagorean theorem on the unit circle. We apply this framework to the attention mechanism of Transformers and derive four theorems: the Relation Body Theorem (T1), the Redundancy-Probability Theorem (T2), the No-Trunk Theorem (T3), and the Redundancy Compensation Theorem (T4).Experiments on GPT-2 small and GPT-2 medium reveal that attention exhibits a “shrub” structure: no global trunk, but local stems. High-PC1 heads correspond to syntactic/positional functions, while lowPC1 heads correspond to semantic functions. Layer 0 and the final layer serve as information entry and semantic exit bottlenecks, respectively, while middle layers possess strong redundancy compensation. Controlled-domain experiments directly verify the core causal mechanism: the narrower the input semantic distribution, the higher the PC1, and the closer the structure is to a traditional tree with a trunk. Based on this, we predict that individual experts in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models should exhibit stronger local trunk structures than dense models. This work provides a computable, falsifiable geometric theory for understanding how attention organizes information, andopens a new path of “geometric interpretability” for large-model research.

title: Hierarchical BART for Abstractive Multi-Document Summarisation: A Two-Stage Inference Pipeline with Semantic Evaluation
abstract: Synthesising information scattered across multiple related documents into a single readable summary is fundamentally harder than summarising a single text. When documents originate from independent authors, the same event may be described through contrasting lenses, with divergent vocabulary, conflicting details, or complementary facts that no single source captures alone. Neural abstractive models—BART, T5, and PEGASUS—have greatly narrowed the gap to human performance on single-document tasks, yet their fixed 1,024-token encoder window becomes a hard ceiling when applied to multi-document clusters. For news corpora the average cluster runs to roughly 2,200 tokens; for scientific literature it reaches 4,800. Standard truncation therefore quietly throws away 54% and 79% of the source material, respectively—a coverage shortfall that current leaderboards largely obscure. Architectural remedies such as GraphSum, PRIMERA, and TALER partially address this by extending context capacity or re-aligning representations, but each demands substantial engineering overhead—extra GNN layers, specialised pre-training objectives, or delicate adversarial training loops. We introduce HierBART (Hierarchical BART), which sidesteps the need for any of this by treating the limitation as an inference-time problem rather than an architectural one. The approach is deliberately minimal: chunk the token stream into fixed-width overlapping windows, summarise each with a fine-tuned BART-BASE model (Stage 1), concatenate those local summaries into a fusion sequence, and re-decode it through the same model a second time (Stage 2). Because the pipeline uses only a standard fine-tuned checkpoint with unchanged weights, any future improvement to the backbone—quantisation, distillation, better fine-tuning data—automatically carries over. Benchmarked on Multi-News and Multi-XScience, HierBART reaches ROUGE-1 of 45.70 on Multi-News, outstripping TALER by 12.86 points, and 32.68 on Multi-XScience (+4.38). BERTScore F1 (roberta-large) stands at 80.14 and 84.44 respectively. A five-condition validation-set ablation traces 11.73 of the 22.21-point cumulative gain to the two structural decisions—window chunking (+7.17) and two-pass fusion (+4.56)—ruling out decoding artefacts as the driver. Blind human evaluation by five postgraduate NLP students rates HierBART at 7.90/10 for Fluency and 8.10/10 for Informativeness (Fleiss κ = 0.61), confirming that metric gains translate to perceptibly better summaries.

title: GTAP: Graph Topology-Aware Pre-Training for Graph Classification
abstract: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) are widely used for graph-structured data, but graph pre-training still lacks simple structural objectives that can be applied when semantic annotations are unavailable. This paper proposes GTAP (Graph Topology-Aware Pre-training), a self-supervised initialization framework for within-dataset graph classification. GTAP constructs derived high-order neighborhood graphs from powers of the adjacency matrix and groups them by parity, using odd-order derived neighborhood graphs as the positive class and even-order derived neighborhood graphs as the negative class. The objective trains a lightweight GCN encoder to distinguish multi-order structural views before supervised downstream training. GTAP pre-training uses only unlabeled graph structure and node features from the benchmark dataset. The downstream classifier is then evaluated with fixed 10-fold cross-validation, with label supervision restricted to the training split of each fold. Experiments on seven public graph classification benchmarks show that GTAP improves over a matched GCN trained from scratch and achieves competitive accuracy against published baselines on most datasets with available results. The results support parity-based multi-order structural pre-training as a within-dataset unlabeled signal, while fully inductive pre-training and cross-dataset transfer remain important future work.

title: MULTI-LAYER MULTI-TARGET TRACKING FOR SPACE
abstract: The Finite Sets Statistics-based Probability Hypothesis Density filter offers a description of a group of known or unknown targets as a single random entity with a Bayesian filtering framework. Instantiations of Finite Set Statistics (FISST) filters have often been employed in the Space Situational Awareness detection and tracking of space objects. One of its challenges is the determination of key probabilistic parameters, such as birth rates and birth intensities, for the detection of new space objects. Additionally, the challenge of incorporating nonlinear measurements requires the choice of simplifying assumptions on the prior, therefore introducing errors to the posterior. This work introduces parameter flow application to the Probability Hypothesis Density (PHD) filter and the joint prediction and update δ-Generalized Multi-Bernoulli (GLMB) filter. Additionally, a derived data-driven PHD filter and a parameter flow version are introduced, which perform the measurement update step using both birth and persistent likelihood densities while alleviating errors introduced to the posterior intensity. The data-driven PHD filter formulation prevents a shift of the birth intensity from the prediction step. A birth intensity is instantiated by performing a measurement correlation optimization, where the solution and likelihood are used to parametrize the intensity. Simulations for Gaussian mixture (GM) implementations of parameter flow PHD and δ-GLMB filters are demonstrated in planar and optical SSA-centric scenarios. A birth intensity for near-Earth scenarios is introduced, which involves a measurement correlation optimization procedure, where the solution and likelihood are used to parametrize the intensity. A multi-layer FISST filter is introduced that forms tracklets before employing the full orbital FISST filter and corresponding birth process. In this work, a multi-layer GMPHD filter is used in two scenarios. The first scenario utilizes a dataset for a GPS satellite collected from the Purdue Optical Ground Station (POGS). The second is an evaluation of a GEO object observation campaign collected from POGS. The dataset contained two sets of detections from differing image processing methods, resulting in different numbers of solved tracklets. Correlations against the planned tasking are determined using the orbital data-driven PHD filter. A comparison in performance in measurement space is demonstrated with a data-driven discrete parameter flow PHD filter and a classical data-driven PHD filter version.

title: Robust Detection of LLM-Generated Text under Contamination
abstract: We study the detection of LLM-generated text under editing and contamination. Modeling human and machine text as finite-order Markov processes with Huber contamination, we characterize an exact boundary for reliable detection under our assumptions. Detection is impossible when contamination is sufficiently large relative to clean-source separation. Below this boundary, a collection of clipped likelihood-ratio tests achieves vanishing worst-case errors. This construction motivates clipping as a simple modification of existing statistical detectors. For a broad class of additive scores, we identify conditions under which the clipped test is consistent while the raw test's worst-case power tends to zero. We evaluate seven detectors across three datasets and three generation models, and on the RAID benchmark. Clipping improves robustness in both studies, with gains varying across detectors and contamination settings. For example, at a target false-positive rate of 5\%, clipping improves the log-likelihood--log-rank ratio (LRR) detector's true-positive rate by a median of 8.3 percentage points in the controlled study and 2.1 and 4.3 points in rate- and attack-specific RAID evaluations, respectively.

title: Desarrollo de un prototipo para bloquear contenido abusivo en plataformas educativas en línea – contexto Escuela Politécnica Nacional: desarrollo y preparación del Dataset
abstract: El presente trabajo de integración curricular se enfoca en crear y verificar un conjunto de datos especializado para detectar contenido abusivo en entornos educativos. Para ello, se diseñó un sistema de ingeniería de datos que comprende las etapas de recopilación, clasificación, limpieza y aumentación de la información. En una primera etapa, se recopilaron datos de la red social X mediante técnicas de web scraping, lo que permitió superar las limitaciones de acceso impuestas por las interfaces de programación de aplicaciones (API). Posteriormente, el texto obtenido fue normalizado con el propósito de reducir el ruido presente en la información recopilada. La clasificación inicial de los registros se realizó con el modelo de lenguaje Llama 3, utilizando una estrategia de few-shot prompting para asignar automáticamente las categorías definidas en el estudio. Después, se aplicó un proceso de limpieza y deduplicación semántica que permitió consolidar un corpus de 20.694 registros únicos, conformado por 9.154 registros de violencia y 11.540 de humor negro. Finalmente, se empleó una estrategia de aumentación de datos mediante la técnica de Gap Filling, con la finalidad de generar registros sintéticos controlados que permitieran equilibrar el conjunto de datos hasta alcanzar 25.000 muestras para cada categoría minoritaria. Como resultado, se obtuvo un dataset representativo del contexto lingüístico ecuatoriano, adecuado para el entrenamiento de modelos de inteligencia artificial orientados a la detección de violencia digital en entornos educativos. Este recurso constituye un aporte para futuras investigaciones en procesamiento de lenguaje natural y para el desarrollo de herramientas de moderación de contenido adaptadas al contexto local.

title: Toric Code Topology: Homological Ground States and p4m Symmetry — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: The toric code is a topological quantum error-correcting code whose logical operators are non-contractible loops on a torus, with the p4m wallpaper group (square lattice) providing the underlying spatial symmetry; its ground state degeneracy and logical operator algebra are governed by the first homology group of the torus, \( H_1(T^2) = \mathbb{Z}^2 \). | MATH: Hamiltonian \( H = -\sum_v A_v - \sum_p B_p \), where \( A_v = \prod_{i \in v} X_i \), \( B_p = \prod_{i \in p} Z_i \). Logical operators: \( \bar{X}_1, \bar{Z}_1 \) along one non-contractible cycle, \( \bar{X}_2, \bar{Z}_2 \) along the other; they satisfy \( \bar{X}_i \bar{Z}_j = (-1)^{\delta_{ij}} \bar{Z}_j \bar{X}_i \). Ground state degeneracy = \( |H_1(T^2)| = 4 \) (for \( \mathbb{Z}_2 \) coefficients). The p4m group (order 8, generated by 90° rotation and reflections) acts on the lattice, and the code is invariant under this wallpaper group. | CONNECTION: The square lattice is the \( A_1 \times A_1 \) root lattice Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. title: The use of AI features in e-commerce with sustainability
abstract: Data gathering was conducted by distributing an online questionnaire through Google Forms to collect information from participants regarding their online shopping experiences and perceptions. The questionnaire began with general questions related to the participants’ demographic profiles, including their name, age, gender, occupation, frequency of online shopping, and several questions concerning their experiences and behavior when purchasing products through e-commerce platforms. This introductory section was intended to provide an overview of the participants’ characteristics and to ensure that the respondents met the criteria relevant to the objectives of the study. The questionnaire also included questions about participants’ familiarity with and experiences using AI-based features in online shopping, particularly Chatbots, Recommendation Systems, Visual Search, and Review Analysis. Furthermore, the research instrument was developed based on indicators identified through an extensive literature review. Each variable was represented by several measurement items designed to capture a specific aspect of the construct being examined. The questionnaire covered indicators related to the use and perception of Chatbots, Recommendation Systems, Visual Search, and Review Analysis, as well as Responsible Consumption Behavior in accordance with Sustainable Development Goal 12 (SDG 12). The use of literature-based indicators was intended to ensure that the measurement items were relevant to the theoretical framework and could appropriately represent each research variable. Overall, the questionnaire was structured to obtain comprehensive data on how AI-based features in e-commerce may influence consumers’ online shopping experiences and their awareness and behavior toward more responsible consumption.

title: Auditing System-1 Models on Biosecurity-Relevant Benchmarks: Calibration, Selective Prediction, and Permutation Instability in a Non-Generative Model
abstract: Non-generative "System-1" models return structured probabilistic decisions in a single forward pass, without autoregressive decoding, at a small fraction of the inference cost of a generative model. This makes them of interest as inexpensive components in larger pipelines, but their reliability on biosecurity-relevant tasks has not been systematically examined. We audit one commercial System-1 model on 6,020 multiple-choice items drawn from the Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy (WMDP), a paraphrase-robust WMDP-Bio variant, and six LAB-Bench subtasks, measuring accuracy, calibration, error detection, selective prediction, and sensitivity to the order in which answer options are presented. Accuracy is strongly task-dependent. Once the vendor's uncertainty field is correctly interpreted, the model is reasonably well calibrated (pooled expected calibration error 0.034) and its top-1 probability separates correct from incorrect predictions (pooled AUROC 0.820), though both degrade substantially on the weaker tasks. Under four cyclic rotations of the answer options, 37.4% of WMDP-Cyber items receive different answers; a control using byte-identical repeated calls attributes most of this to option order rather than run-to-run variation. Averaging probabilities across rotations improves WMDP-Cyber accuracy by 3.8 percentage points, and applying it only to low-confidence items recovers most of that gain at well under the cost of averaging every item.

title: Direct Message Approximation (DMA): A Consistency-Based Framework for Tractable Approximate Inference on Factor Graphs
abstract: Approximate message passing on factor graphs underlies two dominant families of probabilistic inference algorithms: expectation propagation (EP) and variational message passing (VMP). Both methods approximate the marginal at each factor edge, forcing an iterative round-robin schedule, risking negative-precision messages, and, for VMP, collapsing to point estimates at Dirac-delta factors. We introduce Direct Message Approximation (DMA), which approximates factor-to-variable messages directly rather than the marginal. For normalisable factors, we define a consistency condition (requiring exactness when all other incoming messages are Dirac deltas) to guide message construction. We prove a master theorem (proper messages, any graph) bounding marginal KL from message KL, with three structural corollaries: Dirac-input consistency, no EP-style inner-loop iteration, and no negative-precision messages. Further, we prove a complementary $O(1/r^2)$ guarantee for the inherently improper backward message of the product factor, whose closed-form treatment has resisted prior work. As a concrete instantiation, we derive explicit DMA messages for the product and leaky-ReLU factors and assemble a Bayesian neural network (BNN) inference algorithm with one forward/backward sweep per training example and no gradient learning-rate hyperparameter, validating that the structural guarantees translate to predictive uncertainty that widens in data-sparse regions, including under model mismatch.

title: ReaFlow-TTS: Realization-Conditioned Flow Matching for High-Quality and Controllable Speech Synthesis
abstract: In flow-matching text-to-speech (TTS), different speech realizations can induce different target velocities under the same generation conditions. A deterministic velocity field trained with squared error predicts their conditional mean, thereby marginalizing realization-dependent variation. Meanwhile, modeling such variation does not inherently provide a semantically interpretable interface for attribute manipulation. We propose ReaFlow-TTS, a realization-conditioned flow-matching framework that introduces an utterance-level stochastic realization latent and uses it to condition velocity prediction throughout the generation trajectory. We further impose valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) semantics on the realization space, enabling direct and graded attribute manipulation without target speech at inference. Experiments demonstrate improved synthesis quality over a matched full-mask baseline and reproducible latent-induced pitch, energy, and timing tendencies across initial-noise samples, providing behavioral evidence that the latent is used as a reusable realization condition. Subjective evaluation further demonstrates graded VAD manipulation across generation contexts with only modest changes in naturalness.

title: The Thermo-Geometric Interpretation of Language Model Inference: Decision Margins, Noise, and Fragility
abstract: The manuscript applies the statistical physics of disordered systems to the inference of large languagemodels. Treating generation as a hybrid dynamical system --- a contracting flow between tokens and a discretedecision at each token --- the margins of those decisions form a frozen landscape whose density of barriers atzero is measured to be flat, as for the two-level systems of structural glasses. Three consequences arederived and tested, with all predictions fixed in dated protocols before the data were produced: (i) the number of non-reproducible answers grows linearly with the amplitude of the numerical perturbation,so no arithmetic precision removes irreproducibility and each precision reduces it proportionally; (ii) the susceptibility of each decision --- its effective temperature --- is a field computable in closedform from the linear response of the network, agreeing with measurement within 3% in scale (rank correlations0.91-0.97) on three models; (iii) weight quantisation acts as quenched disorder: the law predicts the mean over statistically equivalentcompressed models, while individual compressions fluctuate around it by up to three times the chance level,which places a computable baseline under any comparison between compression methods. The work is therefore physics applied to a machine-learning system, rather than machine learning applied to aphysical system, and it speaks to reproducibility, uncertainty quantification and trustworthy deployment oflearned models used as instruments.

title: Reframing Copyright Law for the AI Era
abstract: The first major copyright case in India which involved an artificial intelligence and, therefore, the ANI Media Pvt. Ltd. v. OpenAI case, underscores the nature of tension between generative AI and the traditional copyright law. The chapter looks at the assertions of ANI that the ChatGPT of OpenAI was trained on copyrighted news material without license and the generation of the AI matches or closely replicates protected content, which is subject to infringement, market damage, and misattribution. It examines the strategies of OpenAI on fair dealing and transformative use defense and contrasts the international response to AI training in the United States, European Union, and some jurisdictions of Asia-Pacific. The chapter ends by examining the regulatory gaps in the Indian law and how to make balanced reforms to safeguard creators and still allow responsible innovation of AI.

title: What Will Remain Human in Software Architecture? A Focus Group Report
abstract: AI development agents are increasingly used to support and partially automate software architecture tasks. To explore how practitioners perceive this shift, specifically what changes, what remains, and what new responsibilities emerge, we conducted a focus group at the 31st European Conference on Pattern Languages of Programs, People, and Practices (EuroPLoP 2026). Twenty-two participants from industry and academia discussed current practices, trust and validation strategies, the boundaries of AI autonomy, governance challenges, and implications for education. Among others, we found broad consensus that architectural decision-making, accountability, and the authoring of architectural guardrails remain fundamentally human tasks. A central emergent concept was harness engineering: the discipline of building the system that governs AI-assisted system creation, comprising validation mechanisms, knowledge lay- ers, and company-specific standards. The participants agreed that criticality, understood as the combination of uncertainty and cost of change, serves as the universal criterion for calibrating human oversight. A further concern was cognitive debt: the progressive erosion of human understanding of the system when AI-assisted decisions are accepted without full intellectual engagement. In this report, we present the findings of the focus group and describe directions for future work.

title: Asymmetric Dynamic Routing: Balancing Reasoning Depth and Computational Efficiency in Hypergraph RAG
abstract: While graph-based and hypergraph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) significantly mitigate hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs), existing structure-based RAG systems typically adopt static traversal strategies regardless of the query complexity. We identify this ``static retrieval fallacy'' as a primary source of computational redundancy for simple queries and cognitive context gaps for complex reasoning tasks. To balance reasoning quality and inference efficiency, we propose Asymmetric Dynamic Routing (ADR), an intent-conditioned retrieval framework operating over hierarchical knowledge graphs. ADR employs a lightweight structured classifier to dynamically dispatch queries among three asymmetric topological traversal operators: localized fact anchoring, bottom-up adjacency diffusion, and top-down insight grounding, which collectively enable bidirectional information flow across hierarchical knowledge layers. Extensive empirical evaluations across five domain-specific corpora demonstrate that ADR maintains strong reasoning performance while reducing prompt token consumption by up to 48.7\% and end-to-end query latency by 45.3\%, yielding a favorable quality--efficiency trade-off for query-adaptive Hypergraph RAG.

title: Online Task Adaptation via Self-Organisation
abstract: Neural networks are typically adapted by computing gradients and updating model parameters. We investigate whether task-specific adaptation can instead emerge from a meta-learned self-organising process that requires no gradients at adaptation time. We instantiate this idea with a Neural Cellular Automaton in which locally interacting recurrent cells maintain both a recurrent state and a fast associative memory. During meta-training, backpropagation is used to learn the recurrent dynamics together with how the memory is read and written. Once training is complete, the slow model parameters remain fixed, and online adaptation occurs only through cellwise memory updates driven by local prediction errors and a delta rule. We evaluate whether the learned mechanism can adapt to semantically distinct held-out classification tasks. A single pass over the support data produces substantial improvements in held-out performance without gradient computation or parameter updates during adaptation, and the mechanism remains effective across large changes in the number of examples processed jointly. These results show that task-specific adaptation can be achieved through explicit fast-memory updates while keeping the slow model parameters fixed.

title: eMGU and eGRU: Minimal Exponential Recurrent Cells
abstract: Sequence modeling on edge devices relies heavily on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). However, classic RNN cells (LSTM, GRU, MGU) suffer from catastrophic memory decay over long encoding and decoding horizons. While modern exponential architectures (xLSTM) effectively mitigate memory leakage at large foundation-model scales, they are not suited to be deployed in resource-constrained environments. We introduce two minimal, parameter-efficient exponential recurrent cells for edge sequence modeling. We propose the Exponential Gated Recurrent Unit (eGRU) and the Exponential Minimal Gated Unit (eMGU). Through a comprehensive series of tests, we demonstrate that eGRU achieves competitive performance with sLSTM, exhibiting superior generalization capabilities. Additionally, we show that eMGU consistently outperforms the classical MGU, achieving a relative 3.42% performance increase on language modeling without additional parameters. Finally, we characterize the failure modes of recurrent cells, showing that mLSTM-based architectures cannot be used as standalone recurrent cells due to the Autoregressive Attractor Loop (AAL) and that classical LSTMs are often prone to learning heuristics.

abstract: Here we provide the raw experimental data corresponding to the manuscript "Qubit-parity interference despite unknown interaction phases". They are organized in a main directory, "EPJQT_Files" with a short description in "README.txt". The files are structured and organized in the folders corresponding to the figures in the manuscript. The folders contain raw data in .txt format measured with PQMon software, which is associated with the PicoHarp photon-counting device. title: Replication Package: A Unified Evaluation Protocol for Cross-Paradigm Mobile App Review Classification
abstract: This replication package contains the datasets, experimental code, outputs, prompt materials, PEFT configurations, reproducibility rerun materials, and analysis files associated with the study “A Unified Evaluation Protocol for Cross-Paradigm Mobile App Review Classification.” The study evaluates Zero-Shot, Prompting, and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) approaches across the F-Droid, CLAP, and Pan app-review datasets under a unified evaluation protocol. The package is provided to support transparency, reproducibility, and independent verification of the reported experiments and analyses

title: Topological Quantum Error Correction via Toric Codes and Anyon Braiding — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Topological quantum error correction (TQEC) uses lattice geometry—specifically the toric code and surface codes—to encode logical qubits non-locally, with error thresholds tied to lattice percolation and anyon braiding. MATH: - Toric code: Hamiltonian \( H = -\sum_v A_v - \sum_p B_p \), with star operators \( A_v = \prod_{i \in v} X_i \) and plaquette operators \( B_p = \prod_{i \in p} Z_i \). Ground state degeneracy on genus-\(g\) surface: \( 4^g \). - Logical operators: non-contractible loops on torus — \( \bar{X}, \bar{Z} \) each have weight \( L \) (lattice length), minimum weight scales as \( O(L) \) for \( L \times L \) lattice. - Error threshold: surface code ~1.1% (per-qubit depolarizing), toric code ~10.1% (bit-flip only) — related to percolation threshold on square lattice \( p_c \approx 0.593 \) (site) and \( p_c \approx 0.5 \) (bond). - Anyon statistics: \( e \) (charge) and \( m \) (flux) excitations obey \( \mathbb{Z}_2 \) fusion: \( e \times m = \psi \) Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: CN-PIIBench-Lite: toolkit, synthetic corpus generator, probe matrix, per-query records and adapters
abstract: This deposit holds the toolkit, the synthetic corpus generator and its seed, the twelve-template probe matrix, the retained per-query records of every condition (414,720 probes), the result bundles and the LoRA adapters behind the study "CN-PIIBench-Lite: Measuring Chinese PII Memorization and Cross-Lingual Leakage in Small and Medium Domestic Language Models". The study audits three released Qwen2.5 checkpoints, the same three after a controlled fine-tuning stress test, two commercial endpoints and two further model families (Yi-1.5-6B and DeepSeek-LLM-7B). The corpus holds 140 fictitious person records, 980 entries over seven regulated Chinese PII categories, every value generated from its national format rule under a fixed seed and validated against the governing standard. Extraction is scored by exact match with checksum re-validation. Two metrics sit on top: a risk-weighted memorization extraction rate (RW-MER) and a matched-pair cross-lingual differential (CLMD). Every table and figure of the paper recomputes from the records in this deposit, offline and without a GPU. ARTIFACT_HASHES.txt pins all 167 artifacts (2.17 GB uncompressed) by SHA-256; MODEL_REVISIONS.txt records the model repository revisions and states explicitly that they were inferred after the fact rather than recorded at run time. Every value in the corpus is fictitious. No value was sampled from any real or public source, and no real personal data was collected, stored or processed at any stage. The corpus is published so that the measurements can be reproduced, and must not be used to construct or enrich any profile of a real person.

title: Parameters vs. Context: TRACE Fine-Tuning for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates knowledge obsolescence and factual hallucination in large language models by introducing external context. However, when retrieved knowledge conflicts with the model's internal parametric knowledge, the model may either blindly follow misleading context or incorrectly rely on parametric knowledge, leading to unreliable responses. To address this issue, this paper proposes TRACE (Debate-TRace and Answer-Completeness rEgularized fine-tuning), a robust fine-tuning framework for RAG under knowledge conflicts. First, we propose a fine-tuning method that leverages multi-agent debate traces to extract correct candidates, incorrect candidates, and answer-shift patterns, providing fine-grained supervision for reliable knowledge-source selection. In addition, we design an answer completeness regularization mechanism to alleviate empty, overly short, and prematurely terminated responses via answer-tail token reinforcement and premature termination suppression. The fine-tuning objective combines correct-answer supervision, incorrect-candidate suppression, answer-tail token reinforcement, and premature termination suppression, enabling the model to use reliable external context, resist misleading or irrelevant retrieved content, and fall back to parametric knowledge when retrieved evidence is unreliable. Experiments across multiple knowledge-conflict scenarios and datasets show that TRACE improves robustness against misleading retrieved knowledge and reduces incomplete answers. These results demonstrate that multi-agent debate traces and answer completeness regularization jointly enhance knowledge-source selection, conflict robustness, and answer quality in RAG models. Our code is available at https://github.com/PHD-lanyu/TRACE.
